dependencies.reason: Blueprint baseline patterns and anti-pattern bans.
Suite schema source of truth for contract-suite/1.0, test-gates/1.0, bundle-manifest/1.0.
Test-gates schema + authoring constraints for CI strict.
Constitutional invariants: immutability boundaries, truth preservation, and platform-wide constraints.
Multi-tenancy: org_id sealing, hide-existence semantics, cross-tenant prohibition.
Capabilities/authorization model; DSAR actions are capability-gated + audited, including tiered export capabilities (data.export.c3, data.export.c4).
PII boundary: identity mapping, PII vault exclusivity, joinable identifier classification, cryptoshred primitives, and anti-differencing invariants.
Consent proof ownership; DSAR MUST preserve consent proofs while removing PII linkability per PII-1.
Tracking schema and storage rules; DSAR MUST delete/transform subject-linked raw telemetry.
Export profiles + data-class ceilings; DSAR access exports MUST bind to a C4-regulated export profile.
Archival/destruction semantics; DSAR cryptoshred is destruction-by-unlinkability without mutating immutable facts.
Ledger immutability boundary: postings MUST NOT be mutated or redacted by DSAR.
Immutable order truth boundary: order price snapshots & fulfillment facts MUST NOT be mutated by DSAR.
Immutable price snapshot boundary: DSAR MUST NOT alter historical pricing truth.
Anomaly monitoring and evidence posture for DSAR/PII access.
Canonical error envelope and subcode conventions for DSAR errors.
Governance discipline: break-glass, approvals, and audit retention requirements.
Registry floor parity for type safety even as non-producer.

anonymization_threshold.ownership: PII-1 sets the privacy invariant; BI-1/AN-1 owns reporting implementation but MUST comply.
anonymization_threshold.statement: Aggregates and drilldowns MUST NOT be displayed or exported when any grouping cohort size is less than min_population_size; such results MUST be suppressed or bucketed into 'other'.

approval_pipeline.notes: Support performs validation; org admin/owner approves org-scoped; platform support + super_admin dual control for platform-wide.

approval_requirements: Validation MUST be performed by an actor with IAM capability dsar.validate.
Org-scoped execution approval MUST be performed by an actor with IAM capability dsar.approve_org.
Platform-wide batch approval MUST be performed by an actor with IAM capability dsar.approve_platform_wide_batch AND MUST include explicit multi_org_scope.
Approval MUST be append-only; rejection reasons MUST be stored.

break_glass.prohibition: break_glass MUST NOT bypass identity verification evidence requirements
break_glass.requirement: platform capability dsar.break_glass + post_facto governance review

subject_notification.residuals_trigger: Any retained data due to legal hold, immutable truth boundaries, or anonymized aggregates MUST be disclosed.

cryptoshred_semantics.definition: Destroy linkability by destroying subject identity mappings and envelope keys so that PII vault ciphertext becomes permanently unlinkable to subject_key.

effects.pii_vault: destroy_mapping_and_keys; retain ciphertext only if required by ARCH-1, but make it unlinkable

evidence_required: cryptoshred_execution_receipt with timestamps and executor identity

checks: dsar_case_state MUST be approved at job start
approval record MUST still be valid (not revoked, not expired)
actor MUST still hold required capabilities for request_type
scope MUST remain equal to approved scope (no widening)
dsar_case_state MUST be completed before issuing delivery token
actor MUST still hold required capabilities for request_type
delivery_token MUST be issued to subject channel only (no third-party substitution)

binding_rules: DSAR access exports MUST use export_profile_id dsar_access_export_c4.
The DSAR export profile MUST be a C4 ceiling profile (includes joinable identifiers and vault rehydration).
C2 and C3 profiles MUST NOT be used for DSAR access exports.

evidence_ref_rules: evidence_ref MUST NOT contain PII; it MUST be a reference token or internal id resolvable only within the PII vault/support systems.
captured_by_actor_id MUST be org-scoped actor identity; platform-wide support actions MUST include platform_actor_id and explicit multi_org_scope.

prohibitions: DSAR case records MUST NOT store direct identifiers (email, phone, full name, address, gov_id).
DSAR processing MUST NOT read or export PII without IAM capability + append-only audit entry.
DSAR processing MUST NOT mutate immutable truth sources (LED-1, ORD-1, PRICE-1).
DSAR access exports MUST NOT be produced under C2 or C3 export profiles; DSAR access exports are C4 by definition due to joinable identifiers.

definitions.access_export: Produce a time-limited export of PII scoped to subject_key and org_id.
definitions.erasure_cryptoshred: Destroy linkability to PII via cryptoshred semantics defined by PII-1 without mutating immutable truth.
definitions.restriction_processing: Restrict or pause processing/use of subject-linked data where feasible; does not imply deletion.

request_types.requirement_precedence: If requestor defaults conflict with request_type minimums, the request_type minimum MUST win.

access_export.notes: Access exports include joinable identifiers and vault rehydration; treat as C4 regulated export.

erasure_cryptoshred.notes: Erasure is irreversible unlinkability; require strong verification.

restriction_processing.notes: Restriction does not release full export or irreversibly destroy linkability.

org_admin.notes: Org admin may submit DSAR but MUST NOT bypass support validation; approval requires strict verification evidence.

platform_support.notes: Platform support may submit platform-wide DSAR batches with explicit multi_org_scope; requires super_admin approval.

subject_self.notes: Subject-initiated DSAR MUST be validated by support with verification evidence, then approved by org_admin/org_owner for org-scoped execution.

tenancy.platform_wide_behaviour: platform_wide DSAR MUST execute as a batch of org-scoped DSAR actions; each org_id MUST be enumerated and logged. platform_wide MUST require explicit multi_org_scope and dual-control approval.

platform_wide_scope.rationale: Platform support may need to process DSAR spanning multiple orgs only when authorized.

tenancy.prohibition: System MUST NOT cryptoshred a subject across multiple orgs unless the DSAR case is explicitly platform_wide with the required approvals.

terminology.dsar_case: The authoritative record of a DSAR request lifecycle, including verification, approvals, actions executed, and receipts.
terminology.dsar_request: A request to exercise data subject rights (access/export, erasure/cryptoshred, restriction).
terminology.subject: A natural person whose data is in scope for DSAR processing.
terminology.subject_key: A pseudonymous stable identifier for a subject within an org_id as defined by PII-1.

subcodes.DSAR_ADMIN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED: Admin approval is required before execution.
subcodes.DSAR_ANON_THRESHOLD_VIOLATION: Attempted to display/export aggregate below min_population_size.
subcodes.DSAR_CRYPTOSHRED_FAILED: Cryptoshred job failed; system MUST preserve immutable truth and record failure evidence.
subcodes.DSAR_EXPORT_TOKEN_INVALID_OR_EXPIRED: Export retrieval token expired or already used.
subcodes.DSAR_SUPPORT_APPROVAL_REQUIRED: Support approval is required before execution.
subcodes.DSAR_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED: Verification evidence is missing or insufficient.

immutability_guards: DSAR-1 SHALL NOT permit mutation or redaction of LED-1 postings.
DSAR-1 SHALL NOT permit mutation or redaction of ORD-1 or PRICE-1 immutable snapshots.

summary: Defines deterministic DSAR request lifecycle, identity verification, dual-control approval, export delivery, and cryptoshred orchestration without mutating immutable truth. Patch v1.2.0: binds DSAR access exports to a C4-regulated DATA-1 export profile and requires auth re-check at job start and token issuance.
title: Data Subject Access Request Contract
